subject: Any way to produce a "fingerprint" plot using ggplot2?

messages.author: 2401d0740178cf07
messages.subject: Any way to produce a "fingerprint" plot using ggplot2?
parts:
Dear ggplotter colleagues,

I am examining some meteorological/ecological variables right now and I need to see their hourly and seasonal pattern. One way to facilitate this kind of analysis is via a "fingerprint" plot, for example like the figures on this page: http://www.bgc-jena.mpg.de/~MDIwork/eddyproc/example.php

Basically, what the figures show is the hourly distribution of a given variable across all the months of the year.

Is there any way to mimic this graphic using ggplot2?

I have hourly data that can be reproduced with this code:

-----------------------------------------------------
library(RCurl)
library(ggplot2)

# read sensible heat data
link <- getURL('http://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/27700634/hourly_sample.csv')
data <- read.csv(textConnection(link), header=T, sep=';', stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.string='NaN')

# get date from character
tmp1 <- paste(as.integer(data$hour), ':', data$hour%%1*60, ':00', sep='')
tmp2 <- paste(data$year, data$month, data$day, tmp1, sep='/')
date <- as.POSIXct(strptime(tmp2, '%Y/%m/%d/%H:%M:%S'))

# insert new date and discard old elements
data2 <- subset(data, select = -c(month, day, hour))
data2 <- cbind(date, data2)

# Data is half-hourly, so we need to aggregate (or average) it hourly.
# First, we need to create hourly factors:
data2$hfac <- droplevels(cut(data2$date, breaks='hour'))

#Then, we aggregate by hours (factor)
data3 <- aggregate(cbind(H) ~ hfac, data=data2, FUN=mean, na.action=na.pass)
data3$hfac <- as.POSIXct(data3$hfac)

# For simplicity sake, let's extract only one year - for example 2008
st <- as.POSIXct("2008-01-01 00:00:00")
en <- as.POSIXct("2008-12-31 23:59:59")
data4 <- data3[data3$hfac > st & data3$hfac < en, ]
-----------------------------------------------------

We can take data.frame "data4" as example. How to produce the "fingerprint" graphic above using this data frame?

Thanks in advance for any insight!

Greetings,
--
Thiago V. dos Santos
PhD student
Land and Atmospheric Science
University of Minnesota

messages.author: da357d1a0f57615c
messages.subject: Re: Any way to produce a "fingerprint" plot using ggplot2?
parts:
Would geom_tile do what you want?

Eg:

# convert the times to named lists so we can get at the hour and day separately
data4$hfac = as.POSIXlt(data4$hfac)

ggplot(data=data4, aes(x=hfac$hour, y=hfac$yday, fill=H)) + geom_tile() + scale_fill_gradient(low="green", high="red")

Malcolm
